artDirection: HYBRID + AUTHORED VECTOR. Image generation is BLOCKED on this workspace (403 insufficient_permissions: image_video_generation), so all new art is hand-authored SVG rasterised to PNG — which is actually superior for flat vector: exact hex, zero gradient, precise outline weights, no derivative-work risk. Plants: flatten-pipeline experiment in progress. Original art only; Toca is the bar, never a source.

pieces.name: Toca standard + critic rubric
pieces.note: Rubric grounded in measured pixels from real Toca frames: pure #000000 outlines at ~1.4% of object height, absolutely flat fills (zero gradient/grain), pure white only 1% of pixels, 3-4 hue families, flat two-tone shading at dV 0.08-0.18. 10 scored categories; any category <=6 fails outright.

pieces.name: Three.js foundation (stage/tween/particles/textures/input)
pieces.note: Verified by screenshot: sprites on correct layers, DPR 1.75, 6/6 textures, live tweens, pooled particles, reduced-motion path, 44px hit enforcement, context-loss overlay. Agent found+fixed idle-loop suppression and degenerate-world bugs during its own verification.

pieces.name: Hills / far backdrop
pieces.note: Own pale back-layer palette, no black outline, tiles seamlessly (y(0)==y(2048)).

pieces.name: Dirt plots (empty / hover / seeded)
pieces.note: FIXED by inverting the strategy. Reads unmistakably as tilled soil at 1024px AND at 130px: crumb texture in 4 values, dark planting hollow, ragged edge, and clods shed onto the grass. Now the frame saturation peak (S .568 vs bush .473 / grass .461) so a child can see where to tap. Verified by my own eye on a meadow-green composite.

pieces.name: Sun & moon characters (blink, mood)
pieces.note: Best asset in the batch: six expression states all readable at 110px, each <=3 changed marks, brow angle carrying the emotion. Loses points only for a single character with no blink state.

pieces.name: Critters — flight paths & wing anim
pieces.note: 3 desynced critters, topped up every 3s. Root cause of the empty layer was spawnCritter bailing on document.hidden.

pieces.name: Plant expressions & personality
pieces.note: 6 states + blink; anchors parameterised so ~30 faced plants do not share one face.

pieces.name: Growth animation (seed→sprout→bloom)
pieces.note: Measured at standard: anticipation -11.6% over 133ms, overshoot 1.202x reciprocal, rotation kick unwinding through +1.34deg, layered celebration. Critic marked it do-not-regress.

pieces.name: Plant idle motion & secondary sway
pieces.note: Per-plant random phase AND period; judged in the motion review.

pieces.name: Plant art quality pass (78 plants)
pieces.note: FAN-OUT GATE CLEARED. Kit code proven scale-ready (critic authored escalator plant, narwhal nettle and airplane tree from kit calls alone). Primer rewritten to match code; root_seed/mass_w keyword-only so the silent lean->root_seed trap is now a TypeError; verifier holes closed (single-id runs no longer report a hollow PASS, and plants are auto-enrolled by glob). Bark separated from ground soil so trunks stop competing with the plot for focal weight. 31/31 palette tokens match, zero drift, zero plant art changed.

pieces.name: Tap/press feedback & juice
pieces.gap: Taps on sky, hills, clouds and open grass produce 0 tweens and 0 particles; press cycle has zero rotation kick and zero position pop (both measured exactly 0.000).
pieces.note: Every tap answers incl. empty space; long-press now differentiates (17/83/500ms produce different curves).

pieces.name: Screen transitions
pieces.gap: Title screen is a plain 800ms crossfade and every modal/button uses default ease with no sibling stagger — 26 letter buttons all arrive on one frame.
pieces.note: Title is now scale-and-fade at 420-460ms expoOut; 45ms sibling stagger on letter buttons, choice cards and book rows.

pieces.name: Global colour harmony & grading
pieces.note: Measured median S 0.4201, 2.73% above S0.60, 1.04% in the muddy band, zero gradients across 24 SVGs. Marked do-not-regress.

pieces.name: Whole-game coherence pass
pieces.note: Fresh agent plays the entire game between waves.

pieces.name: Flat-vector world batch (sun, cloud, hill, grass, dirt, shrub)
pieces.gap: The dirt plot — the one thing a child must instantly understand — reads as a bread roll, not soil you can dig into.
pieces.note: Round 3 review: C1 palette now 9 (median S 0.4201 over 6.4M px, 2.73% above S0.60) and depth separation is the strongest system. FAILS on what the shapes SAY: C2 5, C6 6, C7 5. The critic independently reached the same dirt-plot reservation I had deliberately withheld.

pieces.name: Game scene port to Three.js
pieces.note: Motion fixes measured: motion fraction 0.3462 -> 0.9614 (50 of 52 sprites), critters 0 -> 3, press gained rotation 1.497deg + 3.497u pop (both were exactly 0.000), settle 383 -> 300ms, DOM confetti moved to pooled WebGL, zero linear easing remains. Re-critic verifying, and specifically probing whether 96% motion over-corrected into visual noise.

pieces.name: Wire flat art into the running game
pieces.note: CRITICAL PATH: grep proved nothing in js/ referenced art/flat — all 25 world assets and 9 plants were unused and the game still rendered claymation. Building an alias-map override layer so each newly authored asset lights up with a one-line addition.

log.msg: Spawned motion/feel critic (C9 idle life + C10 response & juice) — judgeable independently of the art restyle.
My own read of the running game: a cloud collides with the HUD, clouds muddle the hill depth, and 8 repeated Grow-3-more text signs are heavy for pre-readers (instant tell 27).
Plant pilot COMPLETE: 6 plants + a shared kit expressed in code so 72 downstream plants inherit fixes automatically.
Caught before fan-out: the pilot used the OLD saturated palette (zero new tokens present). Recolouring at the kit source now — this is exactly why we piloted before scaling.
Pilot also caught 2 stale flatten-experiment PNGs with no SVG master (robot rosebush, zombie tree) — being removed so they cannot ship as authored work.
Kit documents 5 authoring traps found the hard way, incl. an evenodd fill-rule bug that put a floating orange disc on the pizza crust.
Motion critic FAILED the scene: C9 6/10, C10 4/10 (auto-capped by linear easing on DOM confetti).
Critic caught a subtle Three.js bug in its OWN method: Sprites rotate via material.rotation, not object3D.rotation.z — it re-measured everything on the correct channel.
Regression found: the critters layer is empty. The pre-port DOM game had butterflies, bees and night fireflies.
Accessibility bug found: reduced-motion mode removes tap squash entirely, so presses give ZERO acknowledgement. Reduced motion must reduce motion, not remove feedback.
Critic was honest that the blind A/B was inconclusive (reference video stalled) rather than inventing a verdict.
Growth animation PASSED at 8/10 and is marked do-not-regress.
Plant recolour COMPLETE: combined median S 0.630 -> 0.479, %>S0.60 59.4% -> 9.2%. Target hit.
Recolour agent caught MY error: the shadow-tone table in FLAT_ART_BRIEF still held old pre-revision hexes, contradicting the Layer-1 table above it. Re-synced.
It also found 2 hardcoded hexes in _build_plants.py bypassing the kit — now named tokens, so all colour flows from one source.
FAN-OUT GATE: critic judging the 6 pilots AND the kit fitness. 72 plants stay queued until this passes.
World art round 3 delivered: median S 0.420, only 1.5% above S0.60.
I independently re-verified both hard bugs rather than trusting the report: seam colour = 0px in all 3 hill layers, hill/foreground shared colours = 0.
Coordination slip of mine: I committed while a builder was mid-flight and swept its in-flight files in. Re-committed the finished state, scoped to art+docs so the running motion agent is untouched.
Fresh critic now judging world art round 3. I am deliberately withholding my own reservation about the dirt plot so the review stays independent — then I will compare.
PLANT GATE: FAIL, KIT NOT READY. Held the gate — this saved 72 wrong plants.
Decisive measurement: apple vs maple silhouette IoU 0.930 at 128px. Same object in three colourways.
Critic caught a statistical trap I had accepted: aggregate saturation passed, but 4 of 6 plants individually breach the ceiling. In game a plant renders alone, not averaged.

Also caught: OL_FINE=7px contradicts the kit own 1.5% rule (sub-pixel ghosting at 128px), sunflower emits 32 strokes at exactly 13.0px (mathematical-stroke tell), and _kit.png has overlapping labels on the very sheet 10 agents will read.
Kit expansion underway: branch primitive, mechanical vocabulary, parameterised mass+foot, blink state, automated IoU + per-plant saturation gates in _verify.py.
Stress test added: the kit must now build robot rosebush, xylophone tree and banana tree, or it is still wrong.
World art round 3: FAIL (C2 5, C6 6, C7 5) — but C1 palette scored 9 and is now do-not-regress.
VALIDATION: the critic independently reached my withheld dirt-plot reservation. I read it as a bathtub, it read it as a bread roll — same finding, reached blind.
Critic RETRACTED four of its own suspicions after checking source, and flagged them so we would not fix what is not broken. That is the behaviour I want.
New findings: prop_seed silhouette merges with its mound (0px gap where 8px required), worm segment ticks render at 0.4px, and all 3 cloud variants share one recipe including the identical drip lobe.
Sharpest structural note: the dirt plot mixes projections — side-on rim with a top-down hole — which is WHY it reads as food rather than ground.
Round 4 building.
Motion fixes COMPLETE and committed. Motion fraction 0.35 -> 0.96; settle 383 -> 300ms; every tap now answers.
Builder used git stash to re-measure the ORIGINAL under identical conditions rather than trusting remembered numbers.

Two real bugs found: spawnCritter bailed on document.hidden (so any player returning from another tab had an empty sky forever), and paintDayNight overwrote plant colour every frame, erasing the reduced-motion acknowledgement.
I independently verified: all JS passes node --check, confetti fully gone from CSS+HTML, zero bare linear easing.
Re-critic spawned with an explicit brief to hunt for OVER-correction — 96% of sprites moving could read as jittery rather than alive.
Session rate limit killed 3 agents mid-flight. Assessed what survived on disk before respawning anything.
Kit expansion had nearly finished: all 3 stress-test plants + new primitives + automated gates were already written.
Ran the gates myself: G1 diversity PASS (worst pair 0.647, was 0.930) and G2 per-plant saturation PASS. Committed.
Confirmed visually that the kit now builds MECHANICAL plants — robot rosebush with panels and bolts, xylophone of graduated bars. It is no longer a foliage kit.
Dirt plot round 4 died mid-fix and now reads as a mountain range. My redirection: stop redesigning the silhouette, put the identity in surface TEXTURE.
Reduced concurrency to 2 Opus agents — the rate limit was self-inflicted.
FAN-OUT GATE round 2: FAIL — but narrow, mechanical, documentation-only. No art needs redrawing.
Kit code CONFIRMED scale-ready: the critic authored 3 of the hardest remaining plants (escalator, narwhal nettle, airplane tree) from kit calls alone with no missing primitive.
Blind A/B reached a genuine TIE at the reference standard — first time.
Killer finding: ten agents read KIT.md, not _kit.py. The doc still publishes the FAILED OL_FINE=7 and documents none of the new branch/rectilinear primitives.

Silent trap proven: docs say trunk_chunky(...lean) but the code 6th positional is root_seed, so two plants both written lean=0 emit byte-identical feet — the shared-foot failure, reintroduced invisibly.

Verifier holes found by adversarial testing: _verify.py <one-id> prints G1 PASS after zero comparisons and exits 0 — the exact command a fan-out author runs. IDS is a hardcoded 9-name list, so plants 10-78 are never enrolled.
Primer fix underway on Sonnet (mechanical, precisely specified); I will verify the doc-vs-code claims myself with greps before any fan-out.
Dirt plot PASSED at round 5. The strategic inversion worked: calm silhouette, identity in surface texture.
Key device: shed clods on the grass — a mass that sheds crumbs is the one thing a loaf, rock or molar never does.
MAJOR GAP FOUND: none of the flat art was wired in. grep -rn art/flat js/ returned nothing — 25 world assets + 9 plants sitting unused while the game rendered the old claymation.
Wiring agent building an ALIAS MAP rather than scattered path edits, so the remaining 69 plants light up one line at a time.
It must also retune sizing: the flat plot is a wide 2.4:1 bed where the old art was a tall dome, and the plot had become the shortest object on screen despite being the primary tap target.
Primer FIXED and verified: KIT.md now matches code, signatures corrected, _kit.png re-laid out, verifier holes closed.
Durable guard added: _check_palette.py reads _kit.py live and fails on ANY hex drift — the second automated gate protecting future agents.
It caught a conflict I introduced: my dirt-plot commit recoloured soil in the brief without updating the kit.
Resolved by separating BARK from ground SOIL — different materials. Trunks must stay cooler or they compete with the plot for the focal weight we deliberately gave it.
Result: 31/31 tokens match, both gates pass (36 comparisons), and zero plant PNGs changed — the rename was purely nominal.
